quest.title: Tales of Time and Wind
quest.description: The witch's dictionary doesn't mention any specific task related to Venti, but you still follow its guidance and search for him around Mondstadt...
quest.rewards_formatted: Hero's Wit x3, Guide to Ballad x3, Mora x30000

chapter.title: Witch's Homework: Of the Waking of Wind

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: ...I'll take that as a yes, then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Venti?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: #Ah, finally! You're here, {NICKNAME}! Do you have a message for me from someone, by any chance?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: There's not a single prophecy about you in that dictionary.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: That's what you were about to say, right?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: #Oh? Just a moment, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hmm... Your curiosity seems as strong as ever, Barbeloth. Alas, my "future" will have to remain absent from your dictionary.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The wind may be happy to let dandelions trace its form, and have poets sing it into verse, but to be contained is hardly its nature.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: So, dear Barbeloth, please do set your pen down. Words heard on the wind are not meant to be recorded on the page.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: If you're truly interested in this legend, allow me to fashion it into a poem. I'll be sure to share it with you ladies at our next tea party.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Barbeloth? She...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hahaha, Barbeloth has always been a reasonable person, and I believe she heard my request.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: As such, our conversation should be free from interruptions for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, Barbeloth was listening in just now? P—Paimon didn't notice a thing...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Well, she is a Hexenzirkel mage. They all have quite a few tricks up their sleeves.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, you noticed right away, and even got her to leave us alone. Doesn't that make you the real master at cards here?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hmm... Given the various practical factors at play, I'd call myself a master — with limits.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There you go, being all secretive again. Well, anyway, there wasn't a single thing about you in that dictionary.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: You being here is enough. Barbeloth's "prophecy" concerning me may be "incomplete," but it's not "incorrect."

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: There's something I need to do, and I could indeed use your help.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hehe, trusty as always. In that case...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: #Could you play a song with me later, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Yep. That's all.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: But, don't worry. This isn't a performance to decide the fate of some consequential event... It's just a duet between friends.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The last time I played this song, the howling gale was my sole audience, and the notes scattered in all directions, leaving only fragments of the melody behind.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: But now, with a friend like you by my side, why should the wind alone bear witness to this music?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Besides, I think my hands will be just that much steadier, playing alongside a trusty friend like you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll play the best I can.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: That's all I ask. Now, let's head to the performance venue. If we follow the breeze, we'll be there in no time.

choices.text: But is that all you need me to do?
Told me to come here and wait.
The mages wanted me to come see you anyway, though.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This island...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is it special?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Not always. It was once an isle like any other — an ordinary, unassuming aggregation of sand and gravel.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: That is, until seeds of stories were brought here by the wind, and cultivated by time.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: And in due course, the wind brought forth new tales, and time caused them to grow into legends.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: #So, with that... Allow me to welcome you in "truth" to this island favored by Time, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: This is the place where Time and Wind met in the distant past.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa... You suddenly sound so serious, Tone-Deaf Bard. Paimon's not sure she's following this conversation anymore, either...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hehe, fret not, dear Paimon! The best stories always start with a bit of suspense and intrigue.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, this island looks kinda familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: But, forceful gales like that are most suited to wiping things clean, not helping things grow.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: So, after a few crises in Mondstadt were resolved, I made the winds gentler — just strong enough to bolster the people in times of need without knocking them off their feet.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Shadows gather in the distance. I'm sure you've felt it, too.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I've heard about the Pyro Archon's face-off with the Ruler of Death, Ronova, and what happened to the Fatui Harbinger, The Captain.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: And that's not even mentioning how Abyssal activity has been encroaching closer and closer to Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I fear the impending crisis may be beyond what humans alone can solve... In light of that, I need to be prepared.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: It's the Anemo Archon's duty to intervene in times of need. As such, I, Barbatos, will bring forth a wind strong enough to disperse whatever storm lies ahead.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: But, if I whip up a gale of such strength in Mondstadt City, it would just turn the place upside down — clothes, hats, the flowers that rest on people's balconies...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: That's why I chose to do it here — the place where I once offered an ode to Time.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Who knows, perhaps Time shows this island special favor precisely on account of my lovely, lovely music.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, so... Is this place really that special? It sure doesn't look like it...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's a tide that ebbs and flows, and a bunch of birds that come and go... It just seems... normal.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Time's impact on things isn't limited to what the eye can see. Think of it like... a ripe Sunsettia.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: If the outer peel remains intact, it's nearly impossible for the average person to tell whether the fruit inside is ripe.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: But even the tiniest hole in said peel will cause the fruit to rot, starting from that spot.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Nestled in the hands of Time, not one "blemish" marks this island's "peel." Thus, Time's influence on its very essence remains hidden to all.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: At the most fundamental level, of course, all things that lack Time's favor will be erased at some point.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: But with the power that remains here, I can leverage Time to draw a boundary around the Wind.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: That way, the outside world won't notice a thing, no matter how powerful of a gale I whip up here.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: #Of course, as the one requesting help, I should offer something in return. That's why I invited you here, {NICKNAME}... So we could perform an ode to Time together.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: #Just let me know when you're ready, {NICKNAME}. Oh, and I can lend you an instrument if you need one.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Once upon a time, I summoned the first winds of freedom on behalf of Mondstadt's people. With the aid of those winds, liberty was returned to all who were owed it.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ah, looks like our music has moved some in our audience to step on stage.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: But that's against concert rules, so let's usher them out.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I told you about this before, remember? About how I encountered "Time" at the Thousand Winds Temple and received some help.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Well, it was because of Time's help that the those first winds of freedom were able to blow so strongly.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: #Alright, that should do it. This was an exquisite performance, {NICKNAME}. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That power you unleashed just now...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ah, don't worry. That power was mine and mine alone. No external help was involved.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Think of it like... tuning a musical instrument so that it might play melodies lovelier still.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hah, so you do have some tricks up your sleeve! What else are you hiding, hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon. How many tricks could I possibly have? I only have two sleeves, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You know that's not what Paimon meant, Tone-Deaf Bard!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hahaha, I have a feeling the wind is gonna be pretty strong today. We should head back to Mondstadt and tell people to hold onto their hats.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thought we'd have to fly super far, but it looks like we're just outside the city...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm ready.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Great. Let's get started.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's something I need to do first...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: No worries. Just come find me when you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: #Just let me know when you're ready, {NICKNAME}. Oh, and I can lend you an instrument if you need one.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm ready.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Great. Let's get started.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's something I need to do first...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: No worries. Just come find me when you're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Just relax, and let the wind lead the way.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: We're almost there.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I understand your love for music, of course...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: But for now, I'm going to have you... leave the premises.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Alright, let's get going.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hahaha, no need to hold your breath. In and out, easy does it.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I let the birds know we would be coming, so we won't run into them.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hmm... We're almost there.
